entities.summary:
Petubastis III was a native ancient Egyptian ruler who revolted against Persian rule in the late 5th century BCE. As Seheruibre Padibastet, he is known for his efforts to reassert Egyptian independence and promote the cult of Amun.

Born into a time of great upheaval, Petubastis III rose to power as a leader of the native Egyptian resistance against Persian occupation. With the support of the priestly class, he launched a series of rebellions against the Persians, who had conquered Egypt in 525 BCE and installed a satrap to govern the country.

Petubastis III's rebellion was notable for its use of guerrilla warfare tactics and its focus on promoting the cult of Amun, which had been suppressed by the Persians. He also implemented a series of economic reforms aimed at reducing Egypt's dependence on Persian trade.

Despite his efforts, Petubastis III ultimately failed to overthrow the Persians and was killed in battle in 466 BCE. However, his rebellion marked an important turning point in Egyptian history, paving the way for later revolts against Persian rule and cementing the cult of Amun as a major force in ancient Egyptian religion.

Petubastis III's legacy is still remembered today, with many historians viewing him as a symbol of resistance against foreign occupation and a champion of Egyptian culture and identity.
